title: Measuring the Urban Glow
transcript: If you stand at the edge of a city after dark, the sky can look brightest in a direction with very few lamps nearby. Our survey team measured that distant glow from open sites. At each site, a tripod held the meter steady. We used a compass to record the direction of the brightest part of the horizon. We also kept a cloud log, because even a thin layer overhead can send scattered light back towards the ground. The clearest pattern emerged on overcast nights, when the difference between the city edge and the rural sites was larger than it was under clear skies. That affects how planners should assess a lighting change. Surveys before and after installation should cover comparable weather conditions if the aim is to isolate the effect of the new lighting.

questions.prompt: Equipment that kept the measuring device steady: ____
questions.explanation: 每个测点都用三脚架固定测量仪。

questions.prompt: Instrument used to identify the direction of the brightest horizon area: ____
questions.explanation: 调查人员用指南针记录地平线上最亮区域的方向。

questions.prompt: The team kept a cloud ____ to record overhead conditions.
questions.explanation: 薄云也能把散射光反射回地面，因此调查人员记录了云况。

questions.prompt: What pattern emerged on overcast nights?
options: The brightness gap between the city edge and rural sites increased.
The brightness gap between the city edge and rural sites narrowed.
The brightness gap was about the same as on clear nights.
questions.answer: The brightness gap between the city edge and rural sites increased.
questions.explanation: 阴天夜晚，城市边缘与乡村测点之间的亮度差比晴朗夜晚更大。

questions.prompt: How should planners compare measurements taken before and after a lighting change?
options: Average all available readings regardless of the weather.
Match the surveys for weather conditions.
Use clear weather before installation and overcast weather afterwards.
questions.answer: Match the surveys for weather conditions.
questions.explanation: 安装前后应在相近的天气条件下测量，以判断新照明本身的影响。
